title: feat(pocket): 2D Pocket runs on the path kernel behind the planner switch
body:
Side branch: side/path-kernel

The first recipe on the path kernel (K6 of #4023): the 2D Pocket runs on the kernel when the planner switch is `new`. With the default switch (`old`) the old pocket planner runs, unchanged.

Writer record: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3752#issuecomment-7211302888

## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/kernel_pocket.rs` (new): the 2D Pocket recipe. It maps the op parameters to one choice for each stage. It plans each Z level with the heights of that level, and the converter (`kernel_emit::emit_levels`) makes the level plans into one toolpath.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/kernel_level.rs` (new): `plan_level`, the stages of one level in the order of the record (guide, order, load, then link and entry for each cut, then the exit). It is not specific to the pocket. The fallbacks and the notes of the stages go to the status line.
- `crates/app/src/operation/planner_switch.rs`: `KERNEL_KINDS = [Pocket]`. Under `new`, `check_engine` lets the 2D Pocket through. Each other phase-1 kind is still refused by name.
- `crates/app/src/operation/generate/run_job.rs`, `generate.rs`: `run_job_on(job, engine)` and `generate_on(world, op, name, engine)`. `run_job` passes the one reading of the process setting (`planner_engine()`). The Pocket arm reads the engine that it gets and calls `pocket_on_kernel` under `new`.
- `crates/app/src/commands/operation/generate.rs`: `GenerateOperation::new_on(world, name, engine)`, the test hook of #4055 for the real command path.
- `crates/app/src/operation/pocket_kernel.rs` (new): the refusals by name under `new` for the options that this recipe does not plan.
- `crates/motion/src/kernel_emit/` (`mod.rs`, `pen.rs`): `LevelPlan::top_z`, the proved material top of a level (`None` is the stock top). The converter still refuses an approach under it (`APPROACH_IN_MATERIAL`) and a level top above the stock top (`BAD_LEVEL_TOP`).
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/kernel_region.rs`: `without_slivers` (the stock less the fig8 band left a loop with all its points on one line, and the selection refused it).
- `crates/pathkernel/tests/laws/kind_pocket.rs` (new), `registry.rs`: the 2D Pocket row is `Moved`, with the real stage planners and the Waterline choices of the pocket.
- `docs/decisions/3752-kernel-pocket-recipe.md`: the decisions.

## In scope and out of scope

What a 2D Pocket does under `CAMCRAFT_PLANNER=new`:

| Strategy | Under `new` |
|---|---|
| Waterline | Kernel: rings of the boundary at the stepover, load control `None` (each cut above the stated load is named), rings linked at depth, each lift named |
| Offset rings | Kernel: rings at the load step, `ConstantEngagement` with `Reach::Rings` (passes inserted where a ring cuts above the load) |
| Zigzag | Refused by name (`KERNEL_POCKET_ZIGZAG`, points to #3753) |
| Auto | The old rule: Waterline for a round outline (kernel), else Zigzag (refused by name, the text says that Auto chose Zigzag) |
| Adaptive | Refused by name (`KERNEL_POCKET_ADAPTIVE`; the old arm refuses it too) |

Also refused by name under `new`: rest machining (#3753), "do not touch" areas (#3754), the corner relief. 3D levels are the 3D Pocket kind, which `check_engine` still refuses under `new`. No silent fallback to the old planner.

The entry: a selected Helix or Ramp is used where the tool must enter material. Plunge asks for an entry outside material (an arc lead in air, a pre-drilled hole, a cleared column). A closed pocket with none of them is refused with `NO_SAFE_ENTRY` and its fix text.

## Old against new (law measures, #4154)

The disc of #3934 and the dog bone of #3741 in the 80 x 50 stock, tool radius 4, one level. Old: the pinned table of `laws_pockets::pocket_2d_readings_of_the_old_planner` (Auto). New: `k6_pocket::pocket_2d_readings_of_the_kernel` (Waterline on the kernel).

| Case | Planner | Lifts (named) | Crossings | Feeds out of reach | Entries: air / column / solid | Over the limit (worst deg) | Full width | Fallback notes | Laws broken |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| disc Inside | old | 18 (0) | 0 | 0 | 1 / 0 / 18 (9 plunge, 9 helix) | 20 (178) | 0 | 0 | link L4 L5 L6 |
| disc Inside | new | 4 (4) | 1 | 6 | 2 / 2 / 1 (1 ramp) | 1205 (173) | 0 | 0 | link L4 L6 |
| disc Outside | old | 18 (0) | 0 | 0 | 1 / 0 / 18 (9 plunge, 9 helix) | 20 (178) | 0 | 0 | link L4 L5 L6 |
| disc Outside | new | 5 (5) | 0 | 10 | 2 / 0 / 4 (4 ramp) | 362 (180) | 172 | 0 | link L4 L6 |
| dog bone Inside | old | 26 (0) | 0 | 0 | 1 / 0 / 26 (13 plunge, 13 helix) | 32 (180) | 1 | 0 | link L4 L5 L6 |
| dog bone Inside | new | 10 (10) | 1 | 6 | 2 / 8 / 1 (1 ramp) | 812 (173) | 0 | 0 | link L4 L6 |
| dog bone Outside | old | 26 (0) | 0 | 0 | 1 / 0 / 26 (13 plunge, 13 helix) | 32 (180) | 1 | 0 | link L4 L5 L6 |
| dog bone Outside | new | 9 (9) | 0 | 2 | 2 / 0 / 8 (8 ramp) | 310 (180) | 103 | 0 | link L4 L6 |

`testdata/models/fig8.step` (EM-0800-4FL, Outside containment, Waterline, stepover 3, stepdown 10, Helix; 3 levels). Old and new on the same op, read by `kernel_route::fig8_kernel_pocket_lifts_are_named` (heavy) and its light twin:

| Start | Planner | Moves | Lifts (named) | Crossings | Entries: air / column / solid | Over the limit (worst deg) | Full width | Laws broken |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Auto | old | 2780 | 18 (0) | 0 | 0 / 3 / 18 (18 helix) | 1236 (180) | 183 | link L6 |
| Auto | new | 27996 | 18 (18) | 6 | 6 / 0 / 15 (15 ramp) | 8595 (180) | 4179 | link L4 L6 |
| Inside | old | - | 24 (0) | 0 | 0 / 24 / 3 (3 helix) | 1521 (180) | 339 | link L6 |
| Inside | new | refused by name (#4324: the order stage cannot restart a ring and keep its circle and lead) | | | | | | |
| Outside | old | 7573 | 96 (0) | 0 | 0 / 3 / 96 (96 helix) | 85 (135) | 0 | link L6 |
| Outside | new | 27996 | 18 (18) | 6 | 6 / 0 / 15 (15 ramp) | 8595 (180) | 4179 | link L4 L6 |

On fig8 the kernel's Auto resolves to Outside (the band reaches the stock edge with air beyond it), so the two rows are the same path. The fig8 spec of the meter has no part outline (the stock box only), so the meter does not judge the part walls here; the verifier does.

The open items, named and not hidden:
- #4260 and #4272: the full-width reads on Outside (172 and 103) are at the stock edge and on the approach of a stay link. The load stage and the #4154 meter read them differently.
- #4300: a feed of the plan crosses the arc lead of an entry. On the disc Inside and the dog bone Inside it is 1 crossing each (move 11 is in the arc lead of the first entry). On fig8 it is 6 (2 on each level): after a lift, the arc lead of the next air entry runs in from the air across the two outer rings cut before it. `Crossing` blocks the post, so the fig8 pocket does not post under `new` yet. The lead runs in stock that the rings cleared before (no gouge). I added this case to #4300.
- #4324 (new): the order stage refuses the fig8 pocket on the Inside start by name.
- Full width and over the limit on fig8 (4179 and 8595 against 183 and 1236): the same class as #4260 and #4272 (the full-width reads at the stock edge on the Outside start), with no load control (Waterline). The kernel path has about 10 times the moves of the old one (chords, not arcs), so the counts are not one to one. This is the largest open item of the recipe.
- "Over the limit": Waterline has no load control by design. The kernel names each read above the stated load (stepover / D) in one status line note. The meter counts each feed move, and the kernel rings are chords, so the count is higher than the old count of arc moves. The worst angle is the same or lower.
- The entries "solid ... ramp": the helix of the entry stage is chords (#4269 decision 5), so the meter reads it as a ramp. That gives the L4 mark (helix asked, ramp read, no fallback note). The entry stage did fly a helix.
- "Feeds out of reach": the arc leads of the air entries (#4254, #4269).
- #4236 (the chain region of a trace) is not reached by this recipe: the 2D Pocket region is a planar region.

## The verifier

On fig8 (app, through the real generate path): no `Gouge`, `RapidInStock`, `RapidInPart` or `PlungeIntoStock`. `FluteShort` and `ShankHit` are on the old path too (the 20 mm flute of EM-0800-4FL is short for the 20.5 mm pocket). The kernel adds 6 `Crossing` findings (#4300), and the post is blocked by them, as the rule says.

`k6_pocket::the_verifier_passes_each_kernel_pocket` runs the verifier of `camcraft-sim` on each kernel pocket of the pins (square pocket and pocket with a round island, Waterline and Offset rings, Auto / Inside / Outside; disc and dog bone, Auto / Inside / Outside). No `RapidInStock`, no `RapidInPart`, no `PlungeIntoStock`, no `Gouge`. The findings that it reports: `Crossing` on the disc Inside and on the dog bone Inside (#4300). On the closed pockets the kernel has no more crossings than the old planner (0 and 0). The Zigzag trial (not in this PR) gave 30 and 48 `Crossing` findings against 0 for the old planner: that is why Zigzag is refused.

## Pins

Motion (`kernel_laws`, `k6_pocket.rs`):
- `pocket_inside_and_outside_cut_the_same_rings`: the square pocket and the pocket with a round island; Auto, Inside and Outside (Waterline) cut the same multiset of rings (`Curve::same_cut`, 1 um, restart and reverse free).
- `pocket_rings_do_not_lift`: 0 lifts on the square pocket; each lift on the pocket with an island (Auto: 5, Outside: 4) has a named reason.
- `pocket_has_no_dead_end_ramp`: each ramp entry descends along its own first cut and ends at its start.
- `a_closed_pocket_without_a_safe_entry_is_refused_by_name`, `the_zigzag_pocket_is_refused_by_name_on_the_kernel`.
- `the_verifier_passes_each_kernel_pocket`, `pocket_2d_readings_of_the_kernel`.

Motion lib: `kernel_emit::tests::a_level_top_lets_the_approach_start_over_the_floor_above`, `kernel_region::tests::kernel_pocket_selection_drops_a_sliver_loop`.

App (`pocket_pass_start`, `kernel_route.rs`):
- `kernel_route_pocket_generates_verifies_and_posts`: a closed pocket through the real generate path with the engine `new`; no blocking verifier warning; it posts with the shipped Fanuc post.
- `kernel_route_default_engine_keeps_the_old_pocket`: the same op with the default engine is the old planner's path, move for move (the command, `generate_on(Old)` and `generate_on(default)`). The fig8 baseline goldens of #4153 (`kernel_baseline`) are unchanged.
- `kernel_route_refuses_what_the_recipe_does_not_plan`: Plunge in a closed pocket (`NO_SAFE_ENTRY`), Adaptive, rest machining; each other phase-1 kind is still refused under `new`.
- `fig8_kernel_pocket_lifts_are_named` (heavy) and `fig8_kernel_pocket_lifts_are_named_light`: fig8, Waterline, old against new with the law measures. Each start is planned or refused by name (Auto must plan); each lift of the kernel is named; the kernel lifts no more than the old planner; the verifier finds no unsafe kind, and `Crossing` (#4300) is the one blocking kind that the kernel adds.
- `offset_pass_start::planner_switch::switch_new_refuses_a_kind_it_does_not_plan_yet`: updated, the 2D Pocket now passes under `new`.

Kernel (`laws`): `registry::each_moved_kind_obeys_every_law` runs L1-L7 and the link rule on the registered 2D Pocket.

The app suite includes the law measure helpers of `camcraft-motion` (`crates/motion/tests/common/law_measure`, `mask_grid`) with `#[path]`. They are test helpers that read a toolpath; no generator of another crate is imported.

## Gate results (final head)

All on head `42a68699e` (the final commit of this PR), Linux, `-j 6`:
- `cargo check --tests` for `camcraft-pathkernel`, `camcraft-motion`, `camcraft-app` (one at a time): clean.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` for the same three crates: clean.
- Quick gate, `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/side/path-kernel` (under `xvfb-run -a`): 463 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. It holds `pathkernel suites: laws`, `motion suites: kernel_laws`, `motion suites: pass_start_levels`, the motion pocket suites, `app suites: pocket_pass_start`, `offset_pass_start` and the other app pocket suites.
- Example catalog by name (in the quick plan, default switch): `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`: ok.
- Light lane, `cargo xtask gate light`: 7 steps, 0 failed (`app light: pocket_pass_start` holds `fig8_pocket_kernel_baseline_light` and `fig8_kernel_pocket_lifts_are_named_light`).
- The targeted heavy step of this P1 under the safety floor: `cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/side/path-kernel --only "app heavy: pocket_pass_start"`: ok (it holds `fig8_pocket_kernel_baseline`, the #4153 goldens of the default switch, unchanged, and `fig8_kernel_pocket_lifts_are_named`).

## Not exercised

- Zigzag, Adaptive, rest machining, "do not touch" and the corner relief on the kernel (refused by name, out of scope).
- A tilted (3+2) frame: the converter refuses a plane that is not the setup XY plane by name (`NOT_SETUP_XY`). No test generates a tilted 2D Pocket under `new`.
- Pre-drilled holes on the kernel route: the holes go into the entry choice, but no pin runs them.
- The example catalog under `new`: the catalog suites ran with the default switch only.

## Decisions

`docs/decisions/3752-kernel-pocket-recipe.md`. The main ones:
- The pass link `Retract` (the `Links::PLANAR` default) and `KeepDown` become "stay down where proved"; only `Clearance` is the user's retract between cuts.
- A lower level enters over the floor of the level above, where the approach of each entry stands on a cut of every level above (else from over the stock top). The first trial (each level from over the stock top) gave a helix through the cut levels and 6 more `Crossing` findings on fig8.
- The verifier gets the pocket area and the air round the stock (`kernel_pocket_reach`), so an air entry is no `Gouge` of the stock edge; the part walls stay judged.
- An incomplete verdict is refused; only a done verdict reaches the post.
- Zigzag waits for #3753.

Changelog: none (the default stays `old`, so no user sees a change; the switch-over PR writes the row).

Refs #3752
